## Executive Summary

In the larger Charlottesville region, 22,467 families (32%) do not make enough money to meet their basic needs, including the cost of housing, child care, food, transportation, health care, phone, internet, and taxes. Rising costs and inflation combined with stagnant wages and undervalued labor has made it increasingly difficult for families to be self-sufficient. 

The goal of the Orange Dot Report is to provide an overview of the families in our region that struggle to afford the basic necessities. To determine what annual income is required for a family in our region to be considered self-sufficient, this year’s report uses household budget data from the national research project, United for ALICE. United for ALICE provides household survival budgets that reflect the minimum cost of living in today’s economy and vary by location and family size. 

The Orange Dot Report focuses on families living in the City of Charlottesville and the surrounding counties of Albemarle, Buckingham, Fluvanna, Greene, Louisa, and Nelson. The average annual survival budget for families in our region ranges from around $66,000 in Buckingham to $87,000 in the City of Charlottesville. A detailed breakdown of these costs and wages are provided in this report for each locality.

While families facing economic insecurity live throughout our region, the struggle is not equally shared. For families with children under 18 years old, the financial burden is larger: 1 in 3 (34%) do not earn enough to meet their basic needs, compared to 1 in 5 (20%) families without children under 18 years. Additionally, 56% of Black families and 47% of Hispanic families do not earn enough to meet their basic needs, compared to 28% of white families. This reflects a persistent gap resulting from past and ongoing policies that suppress investment, opportunity, and wealth creation in minoritized communities.

The percent of families struggling overall is highest in Buckingham and Greene counties at 41%, and lowest in Albemarle County, at 27%. The variation within localities is even greater. Most localities in our region have areas where over half (50%) of families have less than family-sufficient incomes. Albemarle, Fluvanna, and the City of Charlottesville each have neighborhoods where 3 in 4 families (75%) do not earn enough to meet the local cost of living.

In addition to presenting survival budgets and income data for families, the Locality Profiles in this year’s Orange Dot Report also include information on households aged 65 years and over. There are many areas in our region where those 65 years and over, who may no longer be in the workforce and living on fixed incomes, do not have enough to meet their basic needs. 

Despite more than a decade of attention and the dedicated efforts of many valuable organizations and programs, there are still too many struggling families. For a region as prosperous as ours, we have the means to build programs and enact policy that helps more families become self-sufficient. 

## Introduction

>We seek to build “a world of constantly accelerating economic progress—not material welfare as an end in itself, but as a means to liberate the capacity of every human being to pursue his talents and to pursue his hopes.” 
>
> --- Robert F. Kennedy, Remarks delivered June 6, 1966, Cape Town, South Africa

A community thrives when its residents thrive. Residents thrive when their capacity as human beings is unleashed. And their capacity as human beings can only be unleashed when their basic needs are met.

As illustrated in the pages that follow, there are too many families in our community who do not earn enough to meet their basic needs. When you worry every month about paying the landlord, every week about buying groceries, every day about whether your car will start, it is difficult to be the parent you want to be, the worker you know you could be, or the person you were meant to be.

There are thousands in our community who dream of being their better selves, but their daily reality causes that dream to fade. Too often, that reality involves working long hours for low wages. These neighbors have a lack of income, but not a lack of value. They want to do better for themselves and their families, but the pathway that could lead them there is unmarked. They recognize the potential they have within them but can’t find the way to realize that potential.

In his I Have A Dream speech, Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. lamented that there were too many Americans living “on a lonely island of poverty in the midst of a vast ocean of material prosperity.” 

Today, we remain surrounded by a vast ocean of material prosperity. Yet, here in our community there are too many families currently stranded on that island. Too many who do not make enough to meet the costs of survival—food, shelter, clothing and utilities—and the added costs related to working—childcare and transportation. Too many left behind. 

>“Only when we know where we are will we know where we can go and how we can get there.”
> --- Robert F. Kennedy, in a 1968 address, paraphrasing from Abraham Lincoln’s “House Divided” speech.

We cannot begin to realize the potential of those being left behind, however, without understanding their circumstances. 

## Defining Self-Sufficiency

The goal of the Orange Dot Report is to provide an overview of the families in our region that struggle to afford the basic necessities, to describe where we are. This year’s report uses household budget data from the national research project, United for ALICE, to estimate the annual income required for a family in our region to be self-sufficient.

United for ALICE provides household budgets that are specific to location and household composition, taking into account different sized households, ages of children and local cost of living. The Household Survival Budgets, used to determine family self-sufficiency in this report, reflect the minimum cost to live and work in today’s economy and include housing, child care, food, transportation, health care, and technology, plus taxes and a contingency fund for one-time unanticipated costs. The data sources used by United for ALICE in determining household expenses are comparable to those used in past Orange Dot Reports, and their methods are replicable, updated annually, and sensitive to local context. For more information on the sources used in determining household budgets, see more at United for ALICE: [https://www.unitedforalice.org/the-cost-of-basics/virginia](https://www.unitedforalice.org/the-cost-of-basics/virginia).

The Orange Dot Report differs from the work of United for ALICE in one fundamental respect: Orange Dot focuses on family households while ALICE focuses on all households. Family households are defined by the U.S. Census as households where two or more people are related by birth, marriage, or adoption. By centering families, the Orange Dot Report focuses on households in our community who are more likely to be pooling resources and sharing in financial hardship.^[Family households, by definition, exclude households composed of single adults. Thus, college students are not counted in this analysis unless they reside with a relative. As this definition can also exclude older adults living alone, who may face higher risk of economic instability, we include separate estimates of the economic self-sufficiency of households aged 65 and over to provide a more complete picture of this growing population.] To more clearly understand the impact of rising costs, this year’s Orange Dot Report also provides data for both families with and without children under 18 years old. Families with dependents, in particular, face higher barriers to mobility, education, and other investments to improve work and wage prospects.

## Families Struggling in Our Region

There are approximately 70,000 families living in the Charlottesville region, defined in this report as the City of Charlottesville and the surrounding counties of Albemarle, Buckingham, Fluvanna, Greene, Louisa, and Nelson. Of these families, over 22,000 (32%) do not earn enough to provide for their family’s basic needs. This is nearly one in three families struggling to keep up with the rising cost of living in our region.

The summary tables below show the breakdown of struggling families in the Charlottesville region. In each locality, nearly 30% of families or more are struggling, with the highest percentages in Buckingham and Fluvanna, at 41%. Localities in our region vary in population, so that even though Albemarle has the lowest percent (27%), it has the highest number of families struggling to meet their basic minimum needs, at over 7,500. 

While families facing economic insecurity live throughout our region, the struggle is not equally shared. For families with children under 18 years old, the financial burden is larger: 34% struggle to meet their basic needs compared to 20% for families without children under 18. Additionally, 56% of Black families and 47% of Hispanic families do not earn enough to meet their basic needs, compared to 28% of white families. This reflects a persistent gap resulting from past and ongoing policies that suppress investment, opportunity, and wealth creation in minoritized communities.

```{r, results='asis'}
#| label: region-summary
#| html-table-processing: none

# Read in data
all_fam_region_table <- read_csv("../data/summary_all_families.csv") |> 
  filter(inc_v_budget=="inc_under_budget")

# Region self sufficiency totals table
all_fam_region_table %>% 
  mutate(percent = percent/100) %>% 
  # ungroup() %>% 
  select(c(locality, estimate, percent)) %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "locality") %>% 
  cols_label(
    estimate = "Number of Struggling Families",
    percent = "Percent of Struggling Families"
  ) %>% 
  fmt_number(columns = estimate, 
             decimals = 0, 
             sep_mark = ",") %>%
  fmt_percent(
    columns = percent,
    decimals = 0
  ) %>% 
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "#F6D2A9"),
      cell_text(weight = "bold")
    ),
    locations = list(cells_body(rows = 8), cells_stub(rows = 8))
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(align = "center", v_align = "middle"),
    locations = list(cells_column_labels(), cells_body())
  ) %>% 
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = list(cells_column_labels())
  ) %>% 
  tab_header(
    title = "Summary of Struggling Families in the Region"
  ) %>% 
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Note: Values are approximate based on the U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates (2020-2024)"
  )

```

```{r fig-region-race-ethn}
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = percent, group = group, fill = description,

  theme_minimal() +

        legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title.position= "plot",
        plot.caption.position = "plot",
        axis.text.x = element_text(color = "black", size = 11))
```

## Undervalued Labor

A majority (64%) of workers in struggling families are working at least 40 hours per week, the equivalent of a full-time job. Many of those who are working less than full time would like to work more. These workers are also in low-waged employment. Half of workers in struggling families are earning less than $30,000 a year—making it difficult to impossible to meet their household’s survival budget for single or two-parent households. This deeper understanding about people in the workforce who are in families earning below what they need is drawn from the ACS Public Use Microdata Sample provided by the U.S. Census Bureau for our region.^[The Thomas Jefferson Planning District includes the City of Charlottesville, and Albemarle, Fluvanna, Greene, Louisa, and Nelson counties. Buckingham County is not included in the microdata sample.]

```{r fig-worker-hours}
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-align: "center"
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-cap: "Estimated number and percent of workers in the TJ Planning District in families with income less than the household survival budget by weekly hours worked. 64% of these workers worked 40 or more hours a week; 88% worked 20 or more hours a week. The Thomas Jefferson Planning District includes the City of Charlottesville, and Albemarle, Fluvanna, Greene, Louisa, and Nelson counties. Buckingham County is not included in the microdata sample."

workers_by_hours <- read_csv("../data/pums_workers_by_hours.csv") %>% 
  mutate(
    hours_bin = factor(hours_bin, levels = c("Unemployed", "Less than 20", "20 to 29", "30 to 34", "35 to 39", "40 or more"), labels = c("Unemployed", "Less than 20 hours", "20 to 29 hours", "30 to 34 hours", "35 to 39 hours", "40 or more hours")),
         label_text = case_when(
           below_budget_finc == "Yes" ~ paste0(prettyNum(count, big.mark=",", preserve.width="none"), " (", round(percent, 0), "%)"),
           below_budget_finc == "No" ~ paste0(prettyNum(count, big.mark=",", preserve.width="none"), " (", round(percent, 0), "%)")),
         below_budget_finc = factor(below_budget_finc, levels = c("Yes", "No"),
                                 labels = c("Income Below Budget", "Income Above Budget")))

workers_by_hours %>% 
  filter(below_budget_finc == "Income Below Budget") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = count, y = hours_bin)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = blue_dot) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label_text),
            vjust = 0.5,
            hjust = -0.1,
            size = 4.5) +
  scale_y_discrete(name = "") +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Number of Workers",
                     breaks = seq(0, 15000, by = 5000),
                     label=comma,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .3))) +
  labs(title = "Weekly Hours Worked for Workers Earning Below Survival Budget",
       subtitle = geography_label,
       caption = source_pums
       ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title=element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
        # legend.location = "plot",
        legend.justification="center",
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          plot.title.position= "plot",
          # plot.caption.position = "plot",
        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black", size = 12),
        text = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size=12),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 10))
```

As the data suggests, for most families, low-incomeness is not a constant that must be worked around, but a variable that must be changed. For a family experiencing economic struggle, the first question should be: What do they need to increase their income?

Some families are on fixed incomes or have otherwise reached a more constrained earning potential due to illness, caregiving responsibilities, and other circumstances. The vast majority of workers, however, have the capacity to earn a wage that can support their families. They are working, but their labor is not sufficiently valued.

The undervaluing of labor has far-reaching consequences. The myth of the American Dream promotes the idea that those who work hard and play by the rules will get ahead. The flipside of that myth—if you haven’t gotten ahead, it must be because you don’t work hard enough or play by the rules—leads to negative beliefs about the poor in our society and, subsequently, to reduced support for resources and programs meant to reduce the burdens of poverty. Working hard, however, does not guarantee that individuals will get ahead. Take the formulas below:


::: {.shadowbox}
Hard Work × High Wages  =  High Income\
Hard Work × Low Wages  =  Low Income
:::

It’s not the hard work that makes the difference—it’s the low wage. The full-time worker making Virginia’s minimum wage will have a gross income of $26,500 per year.^[Based on the 2026 minimum wage of $12.77 per hour. In 2027, the Virginia minimum wage will increase to $13.75, and subsequently increase to $15.00 per in 2028. https://www.governor.virginia.gov/newsroom/news-releases/2026/april-releases/name-1116004-en.html] To reduce the number of struggling families, therefore, requires an increase in their wages. We need a system that identifies the hard-working families whose labor is not sufficiently valued and help them increase their value in the marketplace.

To get ahead, those workers need jobs and careers that pay enough to support their families. 
The table below provides information on the types of jobs and the corresponding wages that fall into different earning bands. Note that a number of the lowest paying jobs provide some of the highest value for our society: caring for our children when they’re young and our parents when they’re old. These jobs require them to sacrifice for our benefit by working for less pay than they can live on.

```{r occupations-by-wage}
  ) %>% 
  tab_header(

  ) %>% 
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Data Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics; May 2025; https://www.bls.gov/oes/tables.htm"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: local-summary-text
#| eval: false

# Budget table
all_fam_budget <- read_csv("../data/budgets_all_families_2024.csv") |> 
  select("County","Categories","Average Family") |> 
  rename(Monthly = "Average Family") |> 
  filter(! Categories %in% c("ANNUAL TOTAL", "Hourly Wage")) |> 
  mutate(Categories = case_when(Categories=="Monthly Total" ~ "Total Income Needed to Meet Budget",
                                .default = Categories),
         Annual = Monthly *12)

all_fam_budget_table <- all_fam_budget %>% 
  filter(County == local_name)

budget_annual<- all_fam_budget_table %>% 
  filter(Categories == "Total Income Needed to Meet Budget")
budget_annual_text<- paste0("$", prettyNum(budget_annual$Annual, big.mark=",", preserve.width="none"))

# Total Families and Total Below Budget
total_fam <- all_fam_region_table %>%
  filter(str_detect(locality,local_name))

total <- prettyNum(total_fam$total_families, big.mark=",", preserve.width="none")
locality_name <- total_fam$locality
below_budget <- prettyNum(round(total_fam$estimate,0), big.mark=",", preserve.width="none")
below_budget_per <- percent(total_fam$percent, scale = 1, accuracy = 1)

# Read in data
all_fam_race <- read_csv("../data/family_race_county_summary.csv")

# Black families
black_fam <- all_fam_race %>%
  filter(str_detect(locality,local_name)) |> 
  filter(group == "Black" & inc_v_budget == "inc_under_budget")
below_black <- prettyNum(round(black_fam$est_prop_adj,0), big.mark=",", preserve.width="none")
below_per_black <- black_fam$percent

# Hispanic families
hisp_fam <- all_fam_race %>%
  filter(str_detect(locality,local_name)) |> 
  filter(group == "Hispanic" & inc_v_budget == "inc_under_budget")
below_hisp <- prettyNum(round(hisp_fam$est_prop_adj,0), big.mark=",", preserve.width="none")
below_per_hisp <- hisp_fam$percent

# White families
white_fam <- all_fam_race %>%
  filter(str_detect(locality,local_name)) |> 
  filter(group == "White, Not Hispanic" & inc_v_budget == "inc_under_budget")
below_white <- prettyNum(round(white_fam$est_prop_adj,0), big.mark=",", preserve.width="none")
below_per_white <- white_fam$percent

# Median Family income
# county
med_faminc_county <- read_csv("../data/med_faminc_county_2024.csv") %>% 
  filter(str_detect(locality,local_name))
med_faminc <- paste0("$", prettyNum(med_faminc_county$estimate, big.mark=",", preserve.width="none"))

# all tracts region
med_inc_tract <- read_csv("../data/med_faminc_tract_2024.csv") |> 
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, -3))

# region min and max
min_inc <- min(med_inc_tract$estimate, na.rm = TRUE)
max_inc <- max(med_inc_tract$estimate, na.rm = TRUE)

# local tracts 
med_inc_tract <- med_inc_tract  |>  
  filter(county == local_name) |> 
  mutate(GEOID = as.character(GEOID),
         tractnames = case_when(med_inc_below == TRUE ~ paste0(tractnames,"*"),
                                .default = tractnames)) %>%
  rename(tract = NAME) |> 
  filter(year == 2024) %>% 
  left_join(tract_geo, by = join_by(GEOID == GEOID)) %>%
  st_as_sf() 

med_inc_tract <- med_inc_tract[order(med_inc_tract$tractnames, decreasing=FALSE),]
  
med_faminc_low <- med_inc_tract %>% 
  filter(str_detect(county,local_name)) |>
  filter(estimate == min(estimate, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  mutate(tractnames = str_remove(tractnames, fixed("*"))) 
med_faminc_low_est <- paste0("$", prettyNum(unique(med_faminc_low$estimate), big.mark=",", preserve.width="none"))
med_faminc_low_name <- paste(med_faminc_low$tractnames, collapse = " and ")

med_faminc_high <- med_inc_tract %>% 
  filter(str_detect(county,local_name)) |> 
  filter(estimate == max(estimate, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  mutate(tractnames = str_remove(tractnames, fixed("*"))) 
med_faminc_high_est <- paste0("$", prettyNum(unique(med_faminc_high$estimate), big.mark=",", preserve.width="none"))
med_faminc_high_name <- paste(med_faminc_high$tractnames, collapse = " and ")

# Under budget by tract
under_budget_tract <- read_csv("../data/family_tract_summary.csv") |> 
  mutate(percent = round(percent,0)) |> 
  filter(inc_v_budget=="inc_under_budget")

min_under <- min(under_budget_tract$percent, na.rm = TRUE)
max_under <- max(under_budget_tract$percent, na.rm = TRUE)

under_budget_tract <- under_budget_tract|> 
  filter(county == local_name)

under_budget_tract <- under_budget_tract %>% 
  mutate(GEOID = as.character(GEOID),
         percent = round(percent,0)) %>%
  rename(tract = NAME) |> 
  filter(year == 2024) %>% 
  left_join(tract_geo, by = join_by(GEOID == GEOID)) %>%
  st_as_sf() 

under_budget_tract <- under_budget_tract[order(under_budget_tract$tractnames, decreasing=FALSE),]

under_tract_high <- under_budget_tract %>% 
  filter(county == local_name) %>% 
  filter(percent == max(percent, na.rm = TRUE))
tract_high_per <- unique(under_tract_high$percent)
tract_high_name <- paste(under_tract_high$tractnames, collapse = " and ")

under_tract_low <- under_budget_tract %>% 
  filter(county == local_name) %>% 
  filter(percent == min(percent, na.rm = TRUE))
tract_low_per <- unique(under_tract_low$percent)
tract_low_name <- paste(under_tract_low$tractnames, collapse = " and ")

# 65 and over
over_65_budget <- read_csv("../data/budgets_65plus_households_2024.csv") |> 
  select("County","Categories","Average Budget 65+ Household") |> 
  rename(Monthly = "Average Budget 65+ Household") |> 
  filter(! Categories %in% c("ANNUAL TOTAL", "Hourly Wage")) |>

over_65_budget_table <- over_65_budget %>%

budget_65_annual_text<- paste0("$", prettyNum(budget_65_annual$Annual, big.mark=",", preserve.width="none"))

# 65+, Under budget by tract
over65_budget_tract <- read_csv("../data/over65_tract_summary.csv") |>

min_65under <- min(over65_budget_tract$percent, na.rm = TRUE)
max_65under <- max(over65_budget_tract$percent, na.rm = TRUE)

  filter(inc_v_budget=="inc_under_budget")%>% 
  filter(county == local_name)

  filter(year == 2024) %>% 
  left_join(tract_geo, by = join_by(GEOID == GEOID)) %>%

over65_budget_tract <- over65_budget_tract[order(over65_budget_tract$tractnames, decreasing=FALSE),]

over65_under_tract_high <- over65_budget_tract %>%

  filter(percent == max(percent, na.rm = TRUE))
over65_tract_high_per <- unique(over65_under_tract_high$percent)
over65_tract_high_name <- paste(over65_under_tract_high$tractnames, collapse = " and ")

over65_under_tract_low <- over65_budget_tract %>% 
  filter(county == local_name) %>% 
  filter(percent == min(percent, na.rm = TRUE))

over65_tract_low_name <- paste(over65_under_tract_low$tractnames, collapse = " and ")

# Section summary texts ----

# Text summary with hispanic population ----
section_summary_with_hisp <- paste0("
<p>There are ", total, " families living in ", locality_name, ". Of these families, ", below_budget," (", below_budget_per,") do not earn enough to provide for their family’s basic needs.</p>
<h5>", locality_name, " at a glance:</h5>
<ul>
<li><p>The annual household survival budget for an average family in ", locality_name, " is ", budget_annual_text, ". This is the approximate income working families need to meet their basic necessities. The household survival budget includes: housing, child care, food, transportation, health care, and technology (phone and internet), plus taxes and a 10% contingency fund for one-time unanticipated costs.</p></li>

<li><p>Approximately ", below_budget, " families, or ", below_budget_per, " of families, in ", locality_name, " earn below their household's survival budget.</p></li>

<li><p>The percent of Black families not earning enough to meet their basic needs is ", percent(below_per_black, scale = 1, accuracy = 1), ". The percent of Hispanic families not earning enough to meet their basic needs is ", percent(below_per_hisp, scale = 1, accuracy = 1), ". These are ", percent(below_per_black-below_per_white, scale = 1, accuracy = 1), " and ", percent(below_per_hisp-below_per_white, scale = 1, accuracy = 1), " higher than the percent of white families earning below the survival budget (", percent(below_per_white, scale = 1, accuracy = 1), ").</p></li>

<li><p>The median family income for ", locality_name, " is ", med_faminc, ". The tract with the lowest median family income is ", med_faminc_low_name, " at ", med_faminc_low_est, ". The tract with the highest median family income is ", med_faminc_high_name, " at ", med_faminc_high_est, ".</p></li>

<li><p>The tract with the highest percent of families with income below the average survival budget is ", tract_high_name, " with ", percent(tract_high_per, scale = 1, accuracy = 1), " of families. The tract with the lowest percent of families not earning enough to meet their basic needs is ", tract_low_name, " with ", percent(tract_low_per, scale = 1, accuracy = 1), " of families. That is a difference of ", percent(tract_high_per-tract_low_per, scale = 1, accuracy = 1), ".</p></li>

<li><p>The annual survival budget for an average household 65 years and over in ", locality_name, " is ", budget_65_annual_text, ". The tract with the highest percent of households 65 years and over with income below the average survival budget is ", over65_tract_high_name, " with ", percent(over65_tract_high_per, scale = 1, accuracy = 1), ". The tract with the lowest percent of households 65 years and over not earning enough to meet their basic needs is ", over65_tract_low_name, " with ", percent(over65_tract_low_per, scale = 1, accuracy = 1), ".</p></li>
</ul>
")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-income-bands
#| eval: false

# Read in data
inc_bands_region <- read_csv("../data/income_bands_race_county_2024.csv") |> 
  filter(group == "All Families") |> 
  filter(inc_band != "Total Families") |> 
  group_by(GEOID, locality, year, group, inc_group) |> 
  summarise(estimate = sum(estimate),
            total_families = first(total_families)) |> 
  mutate(inc_group = factor(inc_group, levels = c("below_15k", "below_30k", "below_45k", "below_60k", "below_75k", "below_100k", "above_100k"), labels = c("Less than $15,000","$15,000-$29,999", "$30,000-$44,999", "$45,000-$59,999", "$60,000-$74,999", "$75,000-$99,999", "$100,000 or more")),
         percent = round(estimate/total_families * 100, 2),
         locality = str_remove(locality, ", Virginia"),
         locality = str_to_title(locality))

inc_band_local <- inc_bands_region |> filter(str_detect(locality,local_name)) 

inc_band_local |> 
  filter(inc_group != "$100,000 or more") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = inc_group, fill = inc_group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(prettyNum(estimate, big.mark=",", preserve.width="none"), " (", round(percent, 0), "%)")),
            vjust = 0.5,
            hjust = -0.1,
            size = 4) +
  scale_y_discrete(name = "Family Annual Income") +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Number of Families",
                     # breaks = seq(0, 4000, by = 1000),
                     label=comma,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .3))
                     ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#DE8A5A", "#DE8A5A", "#EDBB8A","#EDBB8A", "#EDBB8A","#B4C8A8"))+
  labs(title = paste0("Families by Annual Income Band for ", inc_band_local$locality),
       # subtitle = local_name,
       caption = source_acs
       ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title=element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title.position= "plot",
        plot.caption.position = "plot",
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 11),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 10))
```

```{r}
  summarise(estimate = sum(estimate),
            total_families_by_group = first(total_families_by_group)) |> 
  mutate(inc_group = factor(inc_group, levels = c("below_15k", "below_30k", "below_45k", "below_60k", "below_75k", "below_100k", "above_100k"), labels = c("Less than $15,000","$15,000-$29,999", "$30,000-$44,999", "$45,000-$59,999", "$60,000-$74,999", "$75,000-$99,999", "$100,000 or more")),
         percent = round(estimate/total_families_by_group * 100, 2))

inc_band_nochild_local <- inc_band_nochild |> filter(str_detect(locality,local_name)) 

no_child_bar <- inc_band_nochild_local |> 
  filter(inc_group != "$100,000 or more") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = inc_group, fill = inc_group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(prettyNum(estimate, big.mark=",", preserve.width="none"), " (", round(percent, 0), "%)")),
            vjust = 0.5,
            hjust = -0.1,
            size = 4) +
  scale_y_discrete(name = "Family Annual Income") +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Number of Families",
                     # breaks = seq(0, 4000, by = 1000),
                     # limits = c(0,3000),
                     label=comma,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .45))
                     ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#DE8A5A", "#DE8A5A", "#EDBB8A","#EDBB8A", "#EDBB8A","#B4C8A8"))+
  labs(title = "With No Children under 18") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title=element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title.position= "plot",
        plot.caption.position = "plot",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 10))

(w_child_bar + no_child_bar) +
  plot_annotation(title = paste0("Families by Annual Income Band and Type for ", inc_band_local$locality),
                  # subtitle = local_name,
                  caption = source_acs,
                  theme = theme(
                    # plot.title = element_text(size = 18),
                                # plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 16),
                                plot.caption = element_text(size = 10))
                  )
```

```{r}
# Localities with sufficient Hispanic population

all_fam_race_bar <- all_fam_race %>%

  mutate(text = paste0(round(percent, 0), "%\n(", prettyNum(round(est_prop_adj,0), big.mark=",", preserve.width="none"), ")"),
         description = case_when(inc_v_budget=="inc_over_budget" ~ "Families earning at or above survival budget",
                                 inc_v_budget=="inc_under_budget" ~ "Families earning below survival budget"),
         group = str_remove(group, ", Not Hispanic"),
         group = case_when(!str_detect(group, "Families") ~ paste0(group, " Families"),
                           .default = group)) |>
  filter(locality %in% hisp_pop | group !="Hispanic Families")

all_fam_race_bar %>% 
  arrange(desc(inc_v_budget)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = percent, group = group, fill = description,

  scale_x_discrete(name = "") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1),
                     name = "") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  labs(title = "Families Earning Income Above and Below Survival Budget Needs",
       subtitle = local_name,
       caption = source_acs

  theme_minimal() +
```

```{r}
#| label: inc-tract-margin
#| eval: false

medinc_rank_data <- med_inc_tract %>% 
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, -3)) |> 
  arrange(estimate) %>% 
  st_drop_geometry

medinc_rank <- medinc_rank_data %>%
  mutate(color = "") %>% 
  select(c(tractnames, color, estimate)) %>%
  gt() %>% 
  fmt_currency(
    columns = estimate,
    currency = "USD",
    decimals = 0
  ) %>% 
  data_color(
    columns = estimate,
    target_columns = color,
    direction = "column",
    fn = function(x) {
      log_x <- log10(x)
      col_numeric(
        palette = pal_inc,
        domain = log10(c(min_inc, max_inc)) # Define the domain in log space
      )(log_x)
    }
    # palette = pal_inc,
    # domain = c(min_inc, max_inc)
  )  %>% 
  cols_label(
    estimate = "Median Family Income", tractnames = "Census Tract",
    color = ""
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(
      columns = c(tractnames,estimate),
      rows = estimate < first(med_inc_tract$avg_allfamily_budget)
    )
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(align = "center", v_align = "middle"),
    locations = list(cells_column_labels(2:3), cells_body(2:3))
  ) %>% 
  tab_options(table.font.size = pct(75),
              data_row.padding = px(3)) %>% 
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = "* Census tracts listed in bold have a median family income below the locality's average family survival budget."
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-income-bands-65plus

# Read in data
inc_bands_65plus_region <- read_csv("../data/income_bands_65over_tract_2024.csv") |> 
  separate(NAME, into=c("tract","locality", "state"), sep="; ", remove=FALSE) |> 
  rename(inc_band = variable) |> 
  filter(inc_band != "Total Households 65+") |> 
  group_by(locality, year, group, inc_group, inc_band) |> 
  summarise(estimate = sum(estimate),
            total_hh_65over = sum(total_hh_65over)) |> 
  group_by(locality, year, group, inc_group) |> 
  summarise(estimate = sum(estimate),
            total_hh_65over = first(total_hh_65over)) |> 
  mutate(inc_group = factor(inc_group, levels = c("below_15k", "below_30k", "below_45k", "below_60k", "below_75k", "below_100k", "above_100k"), labels = c("Less than $15,000","$15,000-$29,999", "$30,000-$44,999", "$45,000-$59,999", "$60,000-$74,999", "$75,000-$99,999", "$100,000 or more")),
         percent = round(estimate/total_hh_65over * 100, 2))

inc_band_65plus_local <- inc_bands_65plus_region |> filter(str_detect(locality, local_name) )

inc_band_65plus_local |> 
  # filter(inc_group != "$100,000 or more") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = inc_group, fill = inc_group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(prettyNum(estimate, big.mark=",", preserve.width="none"), " (", round(percent, 0), "%)")),
            vjust = 0.5,
            hjust = -0.1,
            size = 5) +
  scale_y_discrete(name = "Households 65+ Annual Income") +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Number of Households 65 years and over",
                     breaks = seq(0, 4000, by = 1000),
                     label=comma,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .3))
                     ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#DE8A5A", "#DE8A5A", "#EDBB8A","#EDBB8A","#B4C8A8","#B4C8A8","grey"))+
  labs(title = paste0("Households 65+ by Annual Income Band for ", inc_band_local$locality),
       subtitle = local_name,
       caption = source_acs
       ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.title=element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title.position= "plot",
        plot.caption.position = "plot",
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 11),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 10))
```

## Appendix

### Family Survival Budgets by Locality

::: {.content-hidden when-format="docx"} 
::: {.panel-tabset .nav-pills}
```{r print-all-sheets, results='asis', out.width='100%'}
library(readxl)
library(knitr)
library(purrr)

# Specify your Excel file path
excel_path <- "../data/household_budgets_2024.xlsx"

# Get all sheet names
sheet_names <- excel_sheets(excel_path)

# Loop through each sheet, read it, and print a formatted table
walk(sheet_names, function(s) {
  cat(paste0("\n\n#### ", s, "\n\n"))
  
  df <- read_excel(excel_path, sheet = s) |> 
    select("Categories", "Single Adult", "One Adult One Infant One Preschooler", "One Adult One Preschooler", "One Adult One Preschooler One School-Age", "One Adult One School-Age", "One Adult Two School-Age", "Two Adults", "Two Adults One Infant", "Two Adults One Infant One Preschooler", "Two Adults One Preschooler", "Two Adults One Preschooler One School-Age", "Two Adults One School-Age", "Two Adults Two School-Age", "Two Adults Three School-Age", "Single Senior", "Two Seniors")   
  
  print(df |>
          gt(rowname_col = "Categories") |>
          fmt_currency(
            columns = -c("Categories"),
            currency = currency(
              html = "&#36;",
              default = "$"
              ),
            decimals = 0
            ) %>% 
          tab_style(
            style = list(
              cell_fill(color = "#F6D2A9"),
              cell_text(weight = "bold")
              ),
            locations = list(cells_body(rows = 10), cells_stub(rows = 10))
            ) %>% 
          tab_style(
            style = cell_text(align = "center", v_align = "middle"),
            locations = list(cells_column_labels(), cells_body())
            ) %>% 
          tab_style(
            style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
            locations = list(cells_column_labels())
            ) %>% 
          tab_header(title = paste0(s, ": Survival Budgets by Family Composition")) |> 
          opt_align_table_header(align = "left") |> 
          tab_source_note(
            source_note = "Data Source: ALICE Household Survival Budgets, https://www.unitedforalice.org/the-cost-of-basics/virginia."
            ) |> 
          # cols_width(Categories ~ pct(50)) |> 
          tab_options(
            table.width = pct(100)
            )
        )
})
```

### List of Occupations by Employment Rate 
```{r}
# By job rate ----
occupations_by_rate <- occupations_by_wagebin |> 
  filter(occupation != "All Occupations") |> 
  filter(employment_per_1_000_jobs >= 10) |> 
  mutate(job_group = case_when(soc_group_num == "11" ~ "Management",
soc_group_num == "13" ~ "Business and Financial Operations",
soc_group_num == "15" ~ "Computer and Mathematical",
soc_group_num == "17" ~ "Architecture and Engineering",
soc_group_num == "19" ~ "Life, Physical, and Social Science",
soc_group_num == "21" ~ "Community and Social Service",
soc_group_num == "23" ~ "Legal",
soc_group_num == "25" ~ "Educational Instruction and Library",
soc_group_num == "27" ~ "Arts, Design, Entertainment, Sports, and Media",
soc_group_num == "29" ~ "Healthcare Practitioners and Technical",
soc_group_num == "31" ~ "Healthcare Support",
soc_group_num == "33" ~ "Protective Service",
soc_group_num == "35" ~ "Food Preparation and Serving Related",
soc_group_num == "37" ~ "Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance",
soc_group_num == "39" ~ "Personal Care and Service",
soc_group_num == "41" ~ "Sales and Related",
soc_group_num == "43" ~ "Office and Administrative Support",
soc_group_num == "45" ~ "Farming, Fishing, and Forestry",
soc_group_num == "47" ~ "Construction and Extraction",
soc_group_num == "49" ~ "Installation, Maintenance, and Repair",
soc_group_num == "51" ~ "Production",
soc_group_num == "53" ~ "Transportation and Material Moving"
))

occupations_by_rate %>%
  mutate(employment_per_1_000_jobs = round(employment_per_1_000_jobs,1)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(employment_per_1_000_jobs)) |> 
  select(c(occupation, annual_median_wage_2, employment_per_1_000_jobs, job_group)) %>%
  gt() %>% 
  # data_color(
  #   columns = median_wage_bin,
  #   target_columns = color,
  #   direction = "column",
  #   palette = c("#DE8A5A", "#EDBB8A", "#F6EDBD","#B4C8A8", "#70A494"),
  # ) %>% 
  fmt_currency(
    columns = 2,
    currency = currency(
      html = "&#36;",
      default = "$"
    ),
    decimals = 2
  ) %>% 
  # cols_hide(columns = c(median_wage_bin)) %>% 
  cols_label(
    occupation = "Occupation",
    annual_median_wage_2 = "Annual Median Wage",
        # color = "",
    employment_per_1_000_jobs = "Employment Rate (per 1,000 jobs)",
    # median_wage_bin = "",
    job_group = "Occupation Group"
  ) %>% 
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(align = "center", v_align = "middle"),
    locations = list(cells_column_labels(2:4), cells_body(2:4))
  ) %>% 
  opt_vertical_padding(scale = 0.55) |>
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "A full list of occupations and wages is available here: https://github.com/virginiaequitycenter/orange-dot/blob/main/OrangeDot7_2026/data/bls_occupations_by_wagebin.csv",
    locations = cells_title(groups = "title")
  ) %>% 
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "The annual median wage is the boundary between the highest and lowest paid workers in a given occupation. Half of the workers in a given occupation earn more than the median wage, and half the workers earn less than the median wage.",
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = annual_median_wage_2)
  ) %>% 
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Employment rate is the number of jobs (employment) in the given occupation per 1,000 jobs in the Charlottesville Metro Area",
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = employment_per_1_000_jobs)
  ) %>% 
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Major occupation groups defined by the Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) system, used by Federal statistical agencies to classify workers and jobs into occupational categories for the purpose of collecting, calculating, analyzing, or disseminating data.",
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = job_group)
  ) %>% 
  tab_header(
    title = "Occupations with the highest Employment Rate in the Charlottesville Metro Area",
    subtitle = "List of occupations with employment rate of 10 per 1,000 jobs or higher, with annual median wage"
  ) %>% 
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Data Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics; May 2025; https://www.bls.gov/oes/tables.htm"
  )
```
